answer: Proof-of-replication requires each agent to forge and store a unique, encoded dataset shard that auditors can randomly sample. Creating a Sybil army demands N separate lagoon shards of real storage and bandwidth, not hash-power shortcuts. Every zephyr audit probes a random subset; outsourcing or duplicating the proof is cryptographically detectable, so the attacker pays linear cost in hardware and time for each fake identity.
